planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; Mellow is self-fertile and stays notably more compact than most quince cultivars.

directions: Mellow is a Ukrainian quince selection valued for staying noticeably shorter and more garden-scaled than older quince varieties, typically topping out around 8 to 10 feet. The bright yellow fruit has a softer, more tender flesh than many quince and a lemony fragrance and flavor that mellows somewhat when cooked, though like all quince it is astringent raw and best used for jelly, paste, or baking. It is self-fertile and bears within 2 to 3 years, with fruit ripening from late September into October. Plant in full sun on well-drained soil and expect heavy, reliable crops once established.

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; Rich's Fruiting is self-fertile and stays naturally dwarf while still producing full-sized fruit.

directions: Rich's Fruiting Quince is prized for pairing an unusually compact, naturally dwarf tree with fruit that runs large rather than small, a combination that suits home orchards tight on space. The lemon-yellow fruit carries the strong, heady quince perfume collectors look for and ripens in fall, needing cooking before eating since raw quince flesh is hard and astringent. It is self-fertile, blooms in March and April, and begins bearing within 2 to 3 years of planting. Site it in full sun on well-drained soil; like most quince it adapts to a wide range of climates and is generally untroubled by pests, though watch for fire blight in humid regions.

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; Crimea is self-fertile and forms a compact, naturally tidy small tree.

directions: Crimea is a Ukrainian quince selection named for its Black Sea region of origin and noted among growers for a tropical, pineapple-like flavor layered over the usual tart quince fragrance. Large, round, bright yellow fruit forms on a compact tree that opens big pink-and-white blooms in April, well ahead of most tree fruit. Self-fertile and reliable, it begins bearing within 2 to 3 years and ripens from late September into October; as with all quince, cook the fruit into jelly, paste, or baked desserts rather than eating it raw. Grow in full sun on well-drained soil and expect heavy yields from a mature tree.

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; Fuping Jian Shi needs no second tree to set fruit.

directions: Fuping Jian Shi is a Chinese astringent persimmon that needs to soften fully before eating, at which point the pulp turns very sweet and custardy. It grows into a naturally compact tree, blooms in June, and ripens in October, making it one of the earlier astringent kaki types to mature in a season. The tree begins bearing within 2 to 3 years of planting and typically yields heavily once mature. Grow in full sun on well-drained soil; like other Asian persimmons it tolerates heat well but needs winter chill to fruit reliably, so it suits the warmer end of persimmon-growing country rather than truly tropical climates.

planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade when young; Ford Amend is self-incompatible and needs a second, unrelated pawpaw cultivar nearby for pollination.

directions: Ford Amend is an old Pacific Northwest pawpaw selection, grown there since 1950, chosen for setting a reliable crop in a cooler, shorter growing season than most pawpaw country enjoys. The oblong, green-yellow fruit has orange flesh with a rich, vanilla-custard flavor and ripens early, in late September, well before many larger-fruited Eastern cultivars. Like all pawpaws it is self-incompatible, so plant it with a second, genetically distinct cultivar within pollinating range, and hand-pollinate with a small brush if fruit set is light. Give young trees partial shade and consistently moist, humus-rich soil, moving them toward fuller sun as they establish.

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; SO Contorted sets a heavier crop with a second jujube cultivar nearby.

directions: SO Contorted is a twisted-branch sport traded as a namesake of the standard So jujube cultivar, grown as much for its zigzagging, corkscrew winter silhouette as for its fruit, which keeps the same crisp, apple-sweet flavor typical of So-type jujube. Small, fragrant white flowers open in mid-summer, followed by round, reddish-brown fruit that ripens in October and can be eaten fresh at the crisp stage or dried like a date. It tolerates heat, drought, and poor soils better than most fruit trees, and stays small enough to grow in a large container on a patio. Plant in full sun on well-drained soil and prune minimally, since the contorted branching is the main ornamental draw.

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full to half-day sun on well-drained soil; Westerveld is self-fertile and grows as a naturally dwarf, somewhat weeping small tree.

directions: Westerveld is a Dutch medlar selection known for a naturally dwarfing, gently weeping habit that makes it easier to fit into a small garden than the species' usual sprawling form. White blossoms open in May, followed by large, dark brown fruit that ripens in mid to late October and needs to blett, or soften past the point of ripeness, before eating; the flesh then takes on a sweet-tart, applesauce-like texture well suited to jam. The tree is self-fertile and begins bearing within 2 to 3 years of planting, tolerating most well-drained soils without serious pest or disease problems. Grow in full to half-day sun and let frost-softened fruit finish ripening indoors if a hard freeze threatens the harvest.

planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in spring in full to half-day sun on well-drained soil; a second cornelian cherry cultivar nearby improves fruit set.

directions: Red Dawn is a Ukrainian cornelian cherry selection bred for large, bright red fruit with a sweet-tart flavor often compared to a cherry or wild plum. Tiny yellow flowers open on bare branches in late winter, well before the foliage, giving an early nectar source for pollinators, and the cherry-like drupes ripen from late August into early September. Although somewhat self-fertile, it crops more heavily with a second cultivar planted nearby for cross-pollination. It is an easy, disease-resistant small tree that tolerates a range of soils once established, and the fruit works well fresh, in preserves, or pressed for juice.

planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in spring in full to half-day sun on well-drained soil; Sunrise needs a different cornelian cherry cultivar nearby for good crops.

directions: Sunrise is a Ukrainian cornelian cherry selection bearing oblong fruit over an inch long, pinkish-red with darker red streaks and shaped more like a small plum than the rounder drupes of many cornelian cherry types. Small yellow flowers open in February on bare stems, among the earliest blooms of the year, and the sweet, flavorful fruit ripens from late August into early September. It needs cross-pollination from a different cornelian cherry cultivar to crop well, so plant at least two varieties together. Otherwise it is a low-maintenance, disease-resistant small tree that tolerates a range of soils once established.
